events.title: Birth of Charles M. Schulz
events.description: The cartoonist who created Peanuts was born in Minneapolis, Minnesota. His strip introduced Charlie Brown, Snoopy and Lucy to readers around the world.
events.significance: Peanuts ran for nearly 50 years and became one of the most influential and beloved comic strips ever made.

events.title: Casablanca premieres in New York
events.description: The wartime drama starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman had its world premiere in New York City. It arrived as Allied forces were operating in North Africa, where the film is set.
events.significance: Casablanca is widely regarded as one of the greatest films in Hollywood history, and it is still endlessly quoted.

events.title: India adopts its Constitution
events.description: India's Constituent Assembly adopted the country's Constitution. It came into force two months later, on January 26, 1950.
events.significance: The date is now marked each year as Constitution Day in India. The document set up the framework of the world's largest democracy.

events.title: The Brink's-Mat gold robbery
events.description: Six armed men broke into a warehouse at London's Heathrow Airport. They stole about £26 million in gold, diamonds and cash.
events.significance: It was one of the largest heists in British history, and much of the loot was never recovered.

events.title: NASA launches the Curiosity rover
events.description: The Mars Science Laboratory mission lifted off from Cape Canaveral, Florida, carrying the rover Curiosity on its journey to Mars.
events.significance: Curiosity went on to find evidence that ancient Mars had conditions that could have supported microbial life.
